steps.body: The oldest length trick: give one ribbon a head start and it LOOKS longer. Fair comparing means lining the starting ends up first.
steps.narration: The oldest length trick: give one ribbon a head start and it LOOKS longer. Fair comparing means lining the starting ends up first.

widget.prompt: Measure the stick. Align zero with its start, then place 4 one-unit blocks with no gaps or overlaps.
widget.successFeedback: 4 equal blocks cover the stick exactly — same start, no gaps, no overlaps: that count names its length in blocks.
widget.alignFeedback: Line up zero with the object's starting end before measuring.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: The blocks must touch end to end — no spaces and no covering the same part twice.
widget.unitFeedback: Use same-size blocks so every count names the same unit.

predict.prompt: A shorter ribbon starts 3 cubes ahead. Its far end reaches farther. Longer?

options.label: No — the head start is lying

predict.reveal: Far ends only speak truth AFTER the starts are aligned; the head start faked the reach.

cml.actionGoal: Compare fairly — same start line, level seesaw, one sorting rule — for kmd align ends.
invariants: Fair comparison has fixed rules: lengths compare from one same start line, weights compare by which pan sinks, and sorted groups compare by their counts — the anchors for kmd align ends.
misconceptions: Judging length before aligning starts, reading size as weight, or comparing groups by how much space they fill instead of their counts.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the starts were not lined up, could the far ends still settle which is longer?

widget.prompt: To compare two ribbons fairly, what must you do first? Make it fair, then tap the longer ribbon.

items.label: top ribbon
items.feedback: Judged before the starts were lined up — the head start made the top ribbon LOOK ahead. Slide it to the line, then compare far ends.

widget.unalignedFeedback: Looks can trick you — line the ends up first.
widget.missFeedback: Now the starts are lined up — check the far ends again: the ribbon that reaches farther is the longer one.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — same start makes the compare fair.

widget.prompt: Two pencils are compared, but one is pushed forward before measuring. Is that a fair length test?

options.label: No — comparisons need both ends lined up at the same start
options.feedback: Correct — a pushed-forward pencil fakes extra length; matching the starting ends makes the far ends comparable.

options.label: Yes — whichever pencil looks longer wins
options.feedback: A shifted start hides the true length; looking alone cannot undo the shift.

options.label: Yes, as long as both pencils are the same color
options.feedback: Color has nothing to do with length; only where the ends line up matters.

options.label: Pencils can never be compared fairly
options.feedback: They compare fine once both starting ends are lined up — that is the whole fix.
